discovery: Atom interferometry: coherent matter-wave optics with neutral atoms for fundamental tests and precision measurement

nominees.name: Jörg Schmiedmayer
nominees.affiliation: TU Wien (Vienna University of Technology), Austria

motivation: The nominees made the de Broglie wave nature of atoms into a practical tool. In 1991 Pritchard and Schmiedmayer built the first atom interferometer using material nanofabricated gratings. That same year Kasevich, working with Chu, showed that light-pulse atom interferometers can measure gravity and inertial forces with remarkable sensitivity. Atom optics has since grown into a field of its own. Atom interferometers have measured the fine-structure constant, Newton's constant G and the atom's polarizability. They have tested the equivalence principle and probed decoherence. They have also given rise to gravimeters, gradiometers and gyroscopes now used in geophysics and navigation. Schmiedmayer later took matter-wave interferometry onto atom chips and into studies of quantum many-body dynamics. Their work transformed precision measurement, opened new routes for testing fundamental physics, and created quantum sensors that are now being commercialized. It is a rare case of fundamental quantum physics that also became a technology.
